'''Diana Frost Shelstad''' (born August 19, 1947 in [[Sydney]])<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.idref.fr/147084172|title=Shelstad, Diana Frost (1947–)|work=idRef|access-date=2024-07-27}}</ref> is a [[mathematician]] known for her work in [[automorphic forms]].  She is a professor at [[Rutgers University–Newark]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://sasn.rutgers.edu/staff-directory/mathematics-computer-science|title=Staff directory|work=Mathematics and Computer Science|publisher= Rutgers University–Newark|access-date=2024-07-27}}</ref> She earned her doctorate at [[Yale University]] in 1974 studying real reductive algebraic groups.<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=87725 |name=Diana Shelstad}}</ref>

==Research ==

Shelstad has been a key player in the development of the theory of [[endoscopic group|endoscopy]] which is part of [[Langlands program]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Renard | first = David
 | contribution = Endoscopy for real reductive groups
 | isbn = 978-1-57146-227-5
 | mr = 2856368
 | quote = The purpose of this paper is to review Diana Shelstad’s results on endoscopy for real reductive groups
 | pages = 95–141
 | publisher = International Press | location = Somerville, Massachusetts
 | series = Stabilization of the Trace Formula, Shimura Varieties, and Arithmetic Applications
 | title = On the stabilization of the trace formula
 | url = https://www.imj-prg.fr/fa/bpFiles/Renard.pdf
 | volume = 1
 | year = 2011}}</ref> She co-conjectured the [[Fundamental lemma (Langlands program)|fundamental lemma]] with [[Robert Langlands]] in 1984.  After over 20 years, this conjecture was solved by [[Ngô Bảo Châu]] in 2009, thus opening up a wealth of consequences.<ref>{{citation
 | last = DeBacker | first = Stephen
 | contribution = The fundamental lemma: what is it and what do we know?
 | contribution-url = https://scholar.archive.org/work/5pmtzfvjizdvlihnfubl75jr5e
 | doi = 10.4310/CDM.2005.v2005.n1.a5
 | isbn = 978-1-57146-166-7
 | mr = 2459300
 | pages = 151–171
 | publisher = International Press | location = Somerville, Massachusetts
 | title = Current Developments in Mathematics, 2005
 | year = 2007}}</ref>

In 1999, Shelstad developed a theory of [[endoscopic group|twisted endoscopy]] with [[Robert Kottwitz]].  In 2008–9 she completed work on [[endoscopic group|tempered endoscopy]].

==Awards and honors==
In 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|access-date=2013-07-18}}</ref>

==Selected papers ==
* Shelstad, D. Characters and inner forms of a quasi-split group over <math>\R</math>. [[Compositio Mathematica]], 39 (1979), no. 1, 11–45.
* Langlands, R.; Shelstad, D. On principal values on ''p''-adic manifolds. [[Lie group]] representations, II (College Park, Md., 1982/1983), 250–279, Lecture Notes in Math., 1041, Springer, Berlin, 1984.
* Kottwitz, R. and D. Shelstad Foundations of Twisted Endoscopy, Asterisque, vol. 255, 1999 
* Shelstad, D. On geometric transfer in real twisted endoscopy. [[Annals of Mathematics]] 176 (2012), no. 3, 1919-1985.
